Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42908194



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated outcomes and complications of transoral CO2 laser microsurgery (TLM) for hypopharyngeal tumors and its feasibility in ≥ 75-year-old patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 116 patients (without metastases) treated from February 2012 to October 2024 at our hospital. Oncologic outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves (110 patients; median follow-up: 5.3 years). RESULTS: Five-year local control, disease-specific survival, and overall survival rates were 87.8%, 94.6%, and 85.6%, respectively. Postoperative dysphagia, aspiration pneumonia, pharyngolaryngeal edema, and vocal fold paralysis occurred in 9%, 4%, 3%, and 3% of patients, respectively; none required tracheostomy or surgical hemostasis under general anesthesia. The group with a history of head and neck irradiation had higher rates of dysphagia (p = 0.010) and aspiration pneumonia (p = 0.031) than those without. Differences between age groups were nonsignificant. CONCLUSIONS: TLM appears safe and effective for older patients with appropriately selected hypopharyngeal tumors.

item.title: Comparison of Stress-Mediated Vocal Fold Epithelial Effects in Conventionally-Raised and Germ-Free Mice.
item.dc:creator: Venkatraman A, Jacobs K, Thibeault SL
item.description:
Authors: Venkatraman A, Jacobs K, Thibeault SL
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71008
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42907181



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Up to 25% of patients with voice disorders report concurrent psychosocial stress, which has been shown to cause laryngeal microbiome dysbiosis. Microbiome dysbiosis underlies disease pathophysiology in other organs, leading to uncontrolled inflammation via epithelial barrier dysfunction. There is a need to delineate microbial versus nonmicrobial epithelial stress pathways in the vocal folds (VF) in order to clarify how psychosocial stress may contribute to VF epithelial disease. METHODS: C57BL/6 conventionally-raised (CR) and germ-free (GF) adult mice were equally allocated to stressed and unstressed groups (n = 64, 32 per mouse-type/group, equal sexes). Stressed animals completed a validated restraint stress protocol. Following stress, larynges were collected. Outcomes of VF epithelial barrier dysfunction were compared across stressed, unstressed GF, and CR mice. Immunofluorescence/Immunohistochemistry determined protein expression of epithelial adherens junctions, mucins, and proliferation in mid-membranous VF tissue. Transmission electron microscopy assessed VF epithelial permeability. RESULTS: Regardless of microbiota status, stressed animals had reduced protein expression of VF epithelial adherens junctions, mucins (MUC1, 4) and increased epithelial permeability. Presence of microbiota was associated with stress-induced increases epithelial proliferation, observed in CR, but not GF mice. CONCLUSION: Presence of microbiota was associated with stress-induced increase in VF epithelial proliferation. This increased proliferation may represent an adaptive response to damaged cells to maintain epithelial integrity. Collectively, these findings provide a foundation for identifying VF epithelial targets that could be leveraged in probiotic-based therapies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: A Clinical Study of 66 Cases of Sinonasal Malignant Lymphoma: Results of a Single-Institution Study.
item.dc:creator: Inomata K, Naito S, Takayama N, Fujiwara M, Matsumoto Y, Yokoi H
item.description:
Authors: Inomata K, Naito S, Takayama N, Fujiwara M, Matsumoto Y, Yokoi H
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71010
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42907180



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early diagnosis and treatment of sinonasal malignant lymphoma are crucial because of its diverse clinical and imaging findings and poor prognosis associated with certain histological subtypes. However, the markers that predict the diagnosis and prognosis according to the histological subtypes are unclear. This study aimed to identify these markers. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 66 malignant lymphomas diagnosed using biopsy specimens obtained from the nasal cavity and sinus and treated at our institution. Age, sex, main symptom, primary site, disease stage, histopathological type, blood test parameters, follow-up period, treatment details, and prognosis were analyzed. Overall survival was defined as the time from diagnosis to death from any cause. Progression-free survival was defined as the time from diagnosis to disease progression, relapse, or death. Survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. RESULTS: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) was the most common histological subtype (45 patients), followed by extranodal natural killer (NK)/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTL; 15 patients). The 5-year progression-free survival rates were 50.0% for DLBCL and ENKTL for 28.1%. ENKTL was associated with a significantly poorer prognosis than DLBCL. Among patients with sinonasal DLBCL, CD5-positivity tended to have a poorer prognosis. CONCLUSION: Sinonasal malignant lymphoma exhibits heterogeneous clinical behavior according to the histological subtype. CD5-positive sinonasal DLBCL tended to result in worse outcomes. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the prognostic significance of CD5 expression in sinonasal DLBCL. Further studies are needed to clarify its prognostic significance.

item.title: Oncologic Outcomes in p16-Positive Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma With Extranodal Extension.
item.dc:creator: Taylor V, MacKay C, Taylor SM, Trites J, Al Afif A, Mendez A, Rigby MH
item.description:
Authors: Taylor V, MacKay C, Taylor SM, Trites J, Al Afif A, Mendez A, Rigby MH
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71006
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42907157



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Treatment de-escalation in HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is controversial when extranodal extension (ENE) is present. This study evaluated whether pathologic ENE (pENE) presence and extent (microscopic vs. macroscopic) affect survival outcomes in p16-positive OPSCC treated with primary surgery. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with p16-positive OPSCC treated surgically with or without adjuvant treatment from September 2014 to July 2024. Outcomes included overall (OS), disease-specific (DSS), and disease-free survival (DFS). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were compared between groups using log-rank tests. Multivariable analyses used LASSO-selected variables. RESULTS: Among 232 patients, pENE status was reported in 216, forming the primary multivariable cohort. pENE was present in 115 (53.2%); 69.6% were macroscopic. Five-year OS, DSS, and DFS for the full cohort were 88.5%, 94.4%, and 89.0%, respectively. pENE positivity was not significantly associated with DSS (93.3% vs. 94.6%, p = 0.86), DFS (87.7% vs. 91.7%, p = 0.46), or OS (83.2% vs. 93.4%, p = 0.052). Within pENE-positive disease, 5-year OS was 89.8% for microscopic versus 80.2% for macroscopic pENE (p = 0.22). On complete-case adjusted analysis (N = 96), macroscopic pENE had a nonsignificant 3.8-fold higher hazard of death (HR = 3.77, p = 0.063). Exploratory risk-gradient analysis showed worse OS with macroscopic pENE (HR = 3.29, p = 0.046) and clinical ENE (cENE; HR = 5.07, p = 0.040) compared to a pENE-negative/microscopic pENE reference. CONCLUSION: Macroscopic pENE showed a directional association with worse OS, and exploratory analyses suggested a possible risk-gradient with increasing severity from microscopic pENE to cENE. Larger studies are required to determine the clinical significance of pENE extent in surgically treated HPV-associated OPSCC.

item.title: Planned versus accumulated dose in radiotherapy of oropharyngeal carcinoma - Do recurrences occur in unintended cold spots?
item.dc:creator: Lindegaard AM, Enocson H, Georgiev H, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf A, Kristensen CA, Petersen J, Specht L, Tavlayan E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lindegaard AM, Enocson H, Georgiev H, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf A, Kristensen CA, Petersen J, Specht L, Tavlayan E, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111830
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42906639



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) patients treated with radiotherapy (RT) most often occurs within the high-dose target volume. Anatomical changes during RT may potentially lead to unintended target underdosage, which could contribute to the risk of treatment failure. This study aimed to quantify differences between planned and accumulated dose in the regions of later LRR. METHODS: Patients treated with curatively intended RT for OPSCC between 2009 and 2017 at Rigshospitalet with biopsy-proven LRR were identified. Recurrence volumes were delineated on follow up imaging and mapped to the planning CT. The point of origin (PO) of each recurrence was determined using the nidus method. Dose accumulation was performed using synthetic CTs based on daily cone beam CT, followed by recalculation and summation of daily dose distributions. Planned and accumulated doses at the PO were compared. Additional analyses evaluated effect of deformable registration methods. RESULTS: Forty patients with 54 recurrence volumes were included. The accumulated dose was higher than the planned dose in 57% of recurrences. The mean difference between accumulated and planned dose at the PO was - 0.04 Gy (SD: 0.81; 95% CI: -0.26 to 0.18 Gy; p = 0.72). Neither PO localization nor the dose accumulation process was sensitive to the use of an alternative deformation software. CONCLUSIONS: Within the evaluated setting, no evidence was found that regions of later LRR were systematically underdosed. Dose differences were small and within clinically acceptable limits. This suggests that anatomical changes during RT were unlikely to cause clinically relevant compromised target dose coverage.

item.title: Predicting taste alteration in head and neck cancer patients using 3D transformer-based deep learning model.
item.dc:creator: Neh H, MacRae DC, de Vette SPM, van der Hoek L, van Ooijen PMA, Sijtsema NM, Langendijk JA, van Dijk LV
item.description:
Authors: Neh H, MacRae DC, de Vette SPM, van der Hoek L, van Ooijen PMA, Sijtsema NM, Langendijk JA, van Dijk LV
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108192
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42906280



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Taste alteration is a common post-treatment side effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) radiotherapy. Accurate normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models can support treatment planning aimed at reducing side effects that impair quality-of-life. Deep learning (DL) offers opportunities to incorporate full 3D dose, CT, and organofinterest (OOI) data. Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy. MATERIAL/METHODS: Data from 972 patients was used, with the endpoint being moderatetosevere patientreported taste alteration at six months (EORTC QLQH&N35). DL models were trained using 3D dose distributions, planning CT, OOI segmentations and clinical features. A conventional NTCP model using oral cavity mean dose, parotid mean dose, and age served as reference. Attention maps were evaluated for the transformer-based DL model to quantify the model attention to specific regions of the head and neck area. In addition, two cropping approaches for the 3D data were compared. RESULTS: The CNN and transformer DL models performed comparable to the reference NTCP model in the test set (Reference: AUC = 0.71; ResNet: AUC = 0.68; TransRP: AUC = 0.71), though calibration was best for the reference model. Shifting the crop improved DL performance and transformer attention focused on supraglottic and submandibular regions. CONCLUSION: This study showed that the prediction of taste alteration can be achieved using DL models, particularly transformer-based models which, in contrast to CNNs, can account for global features of comprehensive 3D information of dose distribution, CT-images and organs-of-interest segmentations.

item.title: Toward vestibule-specific staging in nasal vestibule squamous cell carcinoma: a single-centre cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Berardinis R, Durante S, Riccio S, Vavassori A, Tagliabue M, Colombi L, Onza M, Giugliano G, Bruschini R, Ruju F, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Berardinis R, Durante S, Riccio S, Vavassori A, Tagliabue M, Colombi L, Onza M, Giugliano G, Bruschini R, Ruju F, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108191
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42906279



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Nasal vestibule squamous cell carcinoma (NV-SCC) lacks a universally accepted, site-specific staging system, limiting comparability across series and potentially influencing treatment selection. We evaluated variation in stage assignment and prognostic performance across four currently used classification systems in a single-centre cohort. METHODS: Patients with previously untreated NV-SCC managed between 2000 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Tumours were restaged according to the UICC/AJCC sinonasal classification, the UICC/AJCC non-melanoma skin cancer classification, Wang's classification, and the Rome classification. Overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and local control (LC) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox regression models explored associations between clinicopathological variables, treatment modality and outcomes. RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were analysed. Restaging showed substantial discordance in stage assignment across systems. UICC-sinonasal staging assigned a considerable proportion of patients to locally advanced categories, whereas Wang's classification concentrated most cases in cT2. The Rome classification appeared to provide a clinically coherent redistribution of early and advanced disease, although overlap between adjacent stages persisted. Bone infiltration showed the most consistent adverse association with OS, DFS, and LC across several staging-based models. Treatment-related associations were observed in selected models but should be considered exploratory because of the retrospective design and non-randomised treatment selection. CONCLUSION: Applying different staging systems to NV-SCC showed considerable discordance in stage assignment and limited discrimination between adjacent categories. Vestibule-specific staging approaches, including the Rome classification, appeared anatomically coherent but require further validation. Bone infiltration was the most consistent adverse prognostic factor and should be considered in future refinements of staging systems.

item.title: The oral-sleep interface: Associations between oral health status and sleep outcomes in Canadian adults.
item.dc:creator: Mistareehi AJ, Hoja I, Mohamoud W, Lieffers JRL, Katselis GS
item.description:
Authors: Mistareehi AJ, Hoja I, Mohamoud W, Lieffers JRL, Katselis GS
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0350313
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42905758



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances and oral health problems are both prevalent public health concerns with substantial impacts on quality of life and systemic health. However, population-based evidence examining the independent associations between multiple dimensions of oral health and multiple sleep outcomes remains limited. This study investigated the associations between oral health indicators and sleep disturbances among Canadian adults using nationally representative survey data. METHODS: We utilized data from adults aged 18 years and older who completed the 2017-2018 Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS). Four oral health indicators were assessed: self-reported oral health, oral pain, bleeding gums, and dry mouth. Four sleep outcomes were examined: short sleep duration, insomnia symptoms, unrefreshing sleep, and difficulty staying awake. Multivariable logistic regression models were used, with progressive adjustment for sociodemographic factors, health status, and health behaviors. RESULTS: All four oral health indicators were significantly associated with most sleep outcomes in the full adjusted model. For short sleep duration, the strongest association was observed for poor oral health (AOR: 1.623). For insomnia symptoms, dry mouth (AOR: 1.904) and oral pain (AOR: 1.826) exhibited the strongest associations. For unrefreshing sleep, oral pain (AOR: 1.937) and dry mouth (AOR: 1.808) were associated with higher odds of reporting unrefreshing sleep. For difficulty staying awake, dry mouth (AOR: 1.720) and oral pain (AOR: 1.701) showed the strongest associations. CONCLUSION: Oral health problems are associated with multiple dimensions of sleep disturbance. These findings highlight the need for integrated care and complementary screening between dental and sleep medicine.

item.title: Nurses' perceptions of an audiovisual material to support patient education on oral health management in diabetes care.
item.dc:creator: Kudoh R, Shibayama T
item.description:
Authors: Kudoh R, Shibayama T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361280
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42905735



Abstract:
Educational support for nurses is essential to promote oral health management education for patients with diabetes. However, few studies have focused on supporting nurses in this context. This study explored the effects of an audiovisual material designed to support nurses' patient education on oral health management in diabetes care. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight certified diabetes nurse educators. Data were analyzed using content analysis. Four main themes emerged: (1) enhancement of nurses' individual learning (8/8 participants), including improved knowledge of the connection between oral health and diabetes; (2) promotion of professional development and reflection (5/8); (3) provision of new insights into patient care (7/8), particularly regarding patient motivation strategies; and (4) identification of implementation considerations in diabetes outpatient settings. The findings suggest that the audiovisual material, designed to complement an existing evidence-based educational guide, was perceived as useful and may support nurses' learning and educational practices related to oral health education for patients with diabetes.

item.title: Using implementation research frameworks to identify facilitators and barriers to implementation of ferric carboxymaltose intravenous iron among moderately anemic postpartum women participating in a trial in India.
item.dc:creator: Charantimath U, Flax VL, Dandappanavar A, Hannan A, Metgud MC, Kavi A, Somannavar M, Goudar SS, Thind S, Frasso R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Charantimath U, Flax VL, Dandappanavar A, Hannan A, Metgud MC, Kavi A, Somannavar M, Goudar SS, Thind S, Frasso R, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359787
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42905700



Abstract:
Postpartum anemia affects approximately 75% of women in India. We conducted this implementation research (IR) related to the use of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) intravenous (IV) iron as part of a trial in anemic postpartum women. The aim of the IR study was to understand potential facilitators and barriers to implementation of single-dose FCM IV iron. This is a mixed-methods study in three secondary-level healthcare facilities in Belagavi, India, designed to explore selected Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research constructs and Proctor's framework elements. Quantitative data were gathered via surveys of postpartum women who received IV FCM (n = 308) and from healthcare workers and administrators (n = 16). Qualitative data included in-depth interviews with 15 women who received IV FCM, 15 family members of women, and 15 healthcare workers and administrators. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and interview transcripts underwent directed content analysis to augment survey findings. Nearly all women believed IV iron made anemia symptoms better, 76% felt the single infusion process was very easy, 58% completely agreed to receive treatment again, and 69% were very likely to recommend treatment to family or friends. Family members were supportive of women receiving FCM. Health workers felt that single dose FCM had comparative advantages over oral iron; however, 4/10 health workers said giving FCM IV iron is harder than oral iron because of the patient monitoring involved and 8/16 health workers and administrators felt there were not enough trained staff to provide the service. Fewer than half of health workers and administrators (7/16) believed their hospital had enough resources to implement IV FCM infusions, and 9/16 said getting the necessary supplies would be a moderate or major barrier. In conclusion, the intervention was well accepted by women and their families and feasible for government health staff within the context of a trial. Future scale up of FCM IV iron would require out-of-pocket costs to be covered by public funding, staff training on the intervention, and strategies, such as dedicated staff or task shifting, to allow for monitoring during and after the infusion.

item.title: Intraoperative Bone Marrow Frozen Sections Reduce Positive Final Margins in Mandibulectomy.
item.dc:creator: Klage AW, Victor MT, Farlow JL, Hou T, Yesensky J, Mantravadi A, Moore MG, Sim MW
item.description:
Authors: Klage AW, Victor MT, Farlow JL, Hou T, Yesensky J, Mantravadi A, Moore MG, Sim MW
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71007
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42905105



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of intraoperative bone marrow frozen section (IBMFS) use on final margin status and survival outcomes in patients undergoing mandibulectomy for squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and non-SCC neoplasms. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was performed of patients undergoing segmental or marginal mandibulectomy for benign or malignant neoplasms between 2009 and 2025. The medical record was reviewed for demographic data, histopathologic disease features, treatment, and outcomes. Univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses were used to evaluate associations between IBMFS and recurrence-free and overall survival among patients with SCC. RESULTS: Of 235 cases, IBMFS were performed in 80.4%. IBMFS analysis was associated with reduced rates of positive final bone margins (1.1% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.014) and overall positive margins (7.9% vs. 19.6%, p = 0.029). Positive IBMFS rate was higher among non-SCC neoplasms than SCC (23.5% vs. 3.5%, p = 0.007), with no significant difference in rate of final positive margins. IBMFS results demonstrated 90.0% sensitivity, 99.4% specificity, and 98.9% concordance with final histopathology. Among SCC patients, IBMFS use was not significantly associated with recurrence-free survival (aHR 0.671, p = 0.320) or overall survival (aHR 0.967, p = 0.923); only nodal disease and age were significantly associated with survival. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, IBMFS use was associated with improved final margin control across tumor types, including non-SCC neoplasms. Although no survival benefit was demonstrated, its association with margin clearance suggests that IBMFS may be a useful intraoperative adjunct in mandibulectomy for head and neck neoplasms.

item.title: Obesity and Pathologic Response to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer: Preliminary Results From a Pilot Study.
item.dc:creator: Truong AA, Chen L, Lee RH, Wu X, Kang H, El-Sayed IH, George JR, Heaton CM, Likhterov I, Chow M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Truong AA, Chen L, Lee RH, Wu X, Kang H, El-Sayed IH, George JR, Heaton CM, Likhterov I, Chow M, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70505
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42904484



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations between obesity and pathologic response to neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted at a single tertiary academic center. We identified 42 patients with HNSCC treated with neoadjuvant ICI with or without chemotherapy. Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2. The primary outcome was any pathologic response (partial, major, or complete response). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess associations between obesity and response, adjusting for smoking status and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. BMI was also analyzed as a continuous variable. Adjusted predicted probabilities of response were estimated across BMI. RESULTS: Seven patients (17%) were obese. Obese patients had lower rates of pathologic response compared to non-obese patients (29% vs. 69%). On multivariable analysis, obesity was associated with decreased odds of response (OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.72; p = 0.021). Increasing BMI was independently associated with lower odds of response, with a 15% decrease per 1 kg/m2 increase [OR 0.85 (0.72-0.99), p = 0.039]. Adjusted predicted probability of response declined from ~85% at BMI 18 to 25% at BMI 40. In a subset of patients receiving immunotherapy alone, increasing BMI remained associated with decreased response [OR 0.66 (0.44-0.99), p = 0.045]. CONCLUSION: In a small pilot cohort, obesity was associated with decreased pathologic response to neoadjuvant ICI in HNSCC. These findings contrast with the "obesity paradox" observed in recurrent/metastatic settings and suggest the relationship between metabolic state and immunotherapy response may be context-dependent. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

item.title: Cost Effectiveness Analysis of the Presto-Trial: A Three-Armed RCT Evaluating Prophylactic Swallowing Exercises in Head and Neck Cancer Patients During (Chemo)radio Treatment.
item.dc:creator: Vergauwen A, Van den Steen L, Baudelet M, Goeleven A, Nuyts S, Nevens D, Massonet H, Duprez F, Van Nuffelen G
item.description:
Authors: Vergauwen A, Van den Steen L, Baudelet M, Goeleven A, Nuyts S, Nevens D, Massonet H, Duprez F, Van Nuffelen G
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70515
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42902836



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research on oropharyngeal head and neck cancer (HNC) patients indicates that prophylactic swallowing exercises (PSE) during (C)RT can positively affect muscle strength, swallowing function and quality of life (QOL). Primary analyses of the PRESTO-trial showed higher adherence rates for PSE when exercising daily with a speech-language pathologist (SLP), compared to self-guided exercises with either an exercise diary or a digital application. Additionally, higher adherence rates were related to greater improvements in swallowing function and QOL. However, given limited healthcare resources, cost-effectiveness analyses are essential to inform the implementation of such rehabilitation strategies in dysphagia care. This secondary analysis of the PRESTO-data compares the costs and health effects of the three different service models: app-based, therapist-led (daily face-to-face, 20 sessions during (C)RT), and paper-led therapy. METHODS: One hundred fifty patients receiving (chemo)radiotherapy (C)RT for oropharyngeal HNC were randomly assigned to one of the three exercise groups. All performing the same PSE protocol. The treatment protocol required daily training during the first 4 weeks of the (C)RT treatment program. Patients in the therapy group thereby received a total of 20 face-to-face therapy sessions. Health outcomes were expressed as utilities based on the EQ5D5L instrument measured at baseline, post (C)RT and 3 months post (C)RT. Costs were estimated from a health service perspective, including staff time, therapy resources and consumables. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated as ΔCosts/ ΔQALYs. RESULTS: No significant between-group differences were found for utilities. Only significant time effects were observed, with a significant decrease in utilities from baseline to post (C)RT and a significant increase from post (C)RT to 3 months post (C)RT. The therapist-led intervention was associated with the highest costs. The app-group intervention was dominated by the paper group in terms of cost-effectiveness as the utilities were comparable but at a higher cost in the app-group. Consequently, the ICER was computed between the paper-group and therapist-group and resulted in € 124 061,54/QALY. CONCLUSIONS: Despite the overall positive HR-QOL effects post 3 months, the daily therapist-led delivery of PSE therapy was not cost-effective relative to paper-based self-management. Under current resource constraints, low-cost delivery models represent the most economically efficient option. Future research should explore whether hybrid or targeted therapist involvement yields better value by preserving clinical benefit while reducing cost.

item.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Hospitalized With Localized, Regional, and Metastatic Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: LoPolito AG, Akhiwu T, Gao MZ, Semprini J, Watts TL, Cannon TY, Osazuwa-Peters N
item.description:
Authors: LoPolito AG, Akhiwu T, Gao MZ, Semprini J, Watts TL, Cannon TY, Osazuwa-Peters N
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70522
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42902813



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a known complication in cancer patients, but data in head and neck cancer (HNC)-particularly distinguishing localized, regional, and metastatic disease-are limited. METHODS: Using the 2016-2020 National Inpatient Sample, we examined adults ≥ 18 years with HNC, excluding patients with another primary malignancy. Metastatic status was categorized as localized, regional, and metastatic. Outcomes included odds of VTE, pulmonary embolism (PE), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), inhospital mortality, and prolonged length of stay (LOS ≥ 7 days). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with these outcomes. RESULTS: Among 62 032 unweighted (310 160 weighted) admissions, 75.0% had localized HNC, 12.7% had regional HNC, and 12.3% had metastatic HNC; 2.6% had VTE (2.4% localized HNC, 2.3% regional HNC, and 4.1% metastatic HNC). Compared with localized HNC, regional HNC was not associated with increased odds of VTE, PE, or DVT, whereas metastatic HNC was associated with higher adjusted odds of VTE (aOR 1.52; 95% CI: 1.30-1.78), PE (aOR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.98), and DVT (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.18-1.83). VTE was associated with increased inhospital mortality (aOR 1.98; 95% CI: 1.64-2.40) and prolonged LOS (aOR 2.14; 95% CI: 1.92-2.39). CONCLUSION: In hospitalized patients, distant, but not regional, metastatic HNC is associated with higher odds of VTE, and VTE is associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes including increased mortality and prolonged LOS.

item.title: Swallowing Outcomes Following Early Treatment of Head and Neck Cancer-Related Lymphedema.
item.dc:creator: Gregor JW, Charney SA, Zacharias SC, Skrove A, Miller M, Lott DG
item.description:
Authors: Gregor JW, Charney SA, Zacharias SC, Skrove A, Miller M, Lott DG
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71011
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42901883



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Head and neck cancer-related lymphedema (HNCRL) is a common, chronic consequence of head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment that contributes to progressive fibrosis, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. Although early intervention is advocated, its association with longitudinal swallow outcomes remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether early HNCRL treatment was associated with improved objective and patient-reported swallowing outcomes following radiation treatment (RT) and/or chemoradiation (CRT). METHODS: Medical records from 110 patients enrolled in a standardized HNC care pathway were retrospectively reviewed. Internal HNCRL was identified in all participants at 3-months post-RT/CRT, when lymphedema treatment was recommended. Seventy-two patients completed treatment with an advanced pneumatic compression device (APCD) or manual lymphatic drainage (MLD), while 38 did not. Swallowing physiology, patient-reported outcomes, and maximum interincisal opening (MIO) were evaluated at baseline, 3-months, and 15-months post-RT/CRT. Longitudinal within- and between-group comparisons were performed. RESULTS: Treated patients demonstrated significantly more favorable longitudinal DIGEST outcomes for overall severity, swallowing safety, and swallowing efficiency (all p < 0.001), greater improvement in EAT-10 (-3.63 vs. +1.13, p = 0.001) and RSI (-5.21 vs. +2.55, p < 0.001), and no significant difference in MIO change (p = 0.259) or cancer recurrence. Associations for DIGEST, EAT-10, and RSI remained significant after multivariable adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Early HNCRL treatment was associated with greater improvements in swallowing physiology and patient-reported swallowing outcomes. These findings support routine HNCRL surveillance and timely intervention within multidisciplinary HNC care pathways.

item.title: Comparison of intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) and intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) for oropharyngeal cancer: efficacy and toxicity differ by outcome measure.
item.dc:creator: You J, You J, Xu B, Zhou Z
item.description:
Authors: You J, You J, Xu B, Zhou Z
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108602
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42901049



Abstract:
AIM: Whether intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) offers measurable clinical benefits over intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) for oropharyngeal cancer remains debated. METHODS: We pooled data from two phase III randomized trials and one matched cohort study comparing IMPT with IMRT and analyzed disease-control, survival, acute toxicity, and nutritional outcomes. RESULTS: The hazard ratio for locoregional recurrence was 1.37 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-3.36, I2 = 0%]; for progression-free survival, 0.90 (95% CI 0.61-1.33, I2 = 0%); and for overall survival, 0.79 (95% CI 0.32-1.98, I2 = 47%). Acute grade 3 dysphagia occurred in 24% of patients receiving IMPT, compared with 40.9% receiving IMRT [risk ratio (RR) 0.65, 95% CI 0.51-0.84, I2 = 0%]. Grade 3 xerostomia or oral/pharyngeal dryness occurred in 19.9% and 32.5%, respectively (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.54-0.95, I2 = 0%). Exploratory nutritional outcomes showed no definitive benefit, including 12-month gastrostomy dependence (RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.08-1.28, I2 = 0%), weight loss ≥20% (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.12-9.38, I2 = 85.7%), and composite nutritional endpoints (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.12-7.07, I2 = 87.7%). CONCLUSIONS: IMPT's primary advantage is reducing acute toxicity, not improving efficacy.

item.title: Fatigue in head and neck cancer survivors after radiotherapy - prevalence, risk factors, and radiation dose correlates.
item.dc:creator: Magnus V, Schäfer S, Tyyger M, Iyizoba-Ebozue Z, Unger D, Tews AM, Boide A, Mehnert-Theuerkauf A, Seidel C, Moustakis C, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Magnus V, Schäfer S, Tyyger M, Iyizoba-Ebozue Z, Unger D, Tews AM, Boide A, Mehnert-Theuerkauf A, Seidel C, Moustakis C, et al.
Journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice | DOI: 10.1007/s11764-026-02143-w
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900449



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the prevalence of fatigue in head and neck cancer survivors and identify associated factors, including potential associations with radiation dose to cerebral organs at risk (OAR). METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included survivors treated with curative radiotherapy between 2005 and 2023 at a tertiary cancer center. Fatigue and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) were assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30. Dosimetric analyses evaluated associations between fatigue and radiation dose to intracranial OAR (brainstem, cerebellum, posterior fossa, medulla, pituitary gland, basal ganglia, hippocampus), including voxel-based analysis (VBA). RESULTS: One hundred fifty-eight patients were included. The most common tumor site was the oropharynx (38.6%). Median time from radiotherapy completion to study participation was 41 (IQR, 22-61) months. The mean fatigue score was 44.7 (SD, 28.0), exceeding the fatigue levels in the age- and sex-adjusted German general population (29.7); 51.3% of patients showed clinically relevant fatigue (≥ 39 points). Fatigue was inversely associated with HRQoL (ρ = - 0.59, p < 0.001), and positively with distress (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001) and fear of cancer recurrence (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). Higher fatigue was found in patients with impaired performance status and in those with laryngeal and hypopharyngeal cancers. Neither cerebral OAR radiation doses nor skeletal muscle mass index was associated with fatigue, and VBA revealed no relevant subregions. CONCLUSIONS: Clinically relevant fatigue affects about half of head and neck cancer survivors. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: The absence of a correlation with cerebral OAR doses suggests that other, probably multifactorial somatic, psychological and lifestyle-related factors play a more central role in the genesis of fatigue than the radiation-related brain exposures investigated.

item.title: Large language model responses to structured textual descriptions of salivary gland imaging findings: impact of contextual enrichment on self-reported diagnostic confidence and reporting behavior.
item.dc:creator: Lazzeroni M, Capaccio P, Estomba CC, Buccichini G, Firetto MC, Pignataro L, Gaffuri M, Carrafiello G, Lavalle S, Salerno VM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lazzeroni M, Capaccio P, Estomba CC, Buccichini G, Firetto MC, Pignataro L, Gaffuri M, Carrafiello G, Lavalle S, Salerno VM, et al.
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10681-3
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900209



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in clinical decision support, yet their behavior when presented with structured textual descriptions of imaging findings, particularly in salivary gland disease, remains poorly defined. The present study was set out to evaluate how the responses of different LLMs change as the textual input is progressively enriched. The models did not receive imaging data; all inputs were text. METHODS: This exploratory, simulation-based observational study assessed 3 LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) across 10 salivary gland cases. For each case, a standardized textual description of the imaging findings was prepared and submitted as a text prompt; no image files were uploaded to any platform. Each case was evaluated under 3 input conditions of increasing informational content: single-plane textual description, multiplanar textual description, and multiplanar textual description plus clinical information, generating 90 total observations derived from repeated measurement of the same 10 cases. Primary outcomes were the model-generated severity score, self-reported diagnostic confidence, and the number of additional reported anatomical structures. AI outputs were not benchmarked against a verified reference diagnosis. The primary analysis was a proportional-odds model with input condition as the fixed effect of interest, AI system as a covariate, and cluster-robust standard errors by case; non-parametric tests were used as sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Model-generated severity scores did not significantly differ among LLMs (χ²=2.31; P = 0.31). Self-reported diagnostic confidence increased significantly as the textual input was enriched (Friedman χ²=18.86; P < 0.001; proportional-odds model, multiplanar description plus clinical information vs. single-plane description, cumulative OR 5.43, 95% CI 3.00-9.81). ChatGPT produced stable outputs with no additional reported structures, whereas Claude produced substantially more detailed reports (mean additional structures, 5.67 vs. 0.00). Gemini produced lower severity scores but comparable self-reported confidence. Mixed-model analysis revealed a significant effect of AI system on reporting verbosity (P < 0.001). Associations between model-reported parenchymal changes and self-reported confidence were also observed; because both variables were generated by the same model within the same response, these represent within-output associations rather than independent diagnostic relationships and are reported descriptively. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory pilot study, LLMs produced comparable severity ratings, while self-reported diagnostic confidence increased as more information was supplied in the prompt. This pattern may reflect the tendency of an LLM to express greater certainty when given richer input rather than genuinely improved diagnostic reasoning. Substantial variability in reporting behavior exists across models, particularly in output detail. These findings suggest that LLMs may warrant further investigation as adjunctive tools for text-based tasks in salivary gland care. The present design does not evaluate image interpretation and does not support use as standalone diagnostic systems.

item.title: Surgical timing in patients with cocaine-induced midline destructive lesions: when and how.
item.dc:creator: Trimarchi M, Landis BN, Simmen D, Saleh H, East C, Herman P, Bussi M, Robotti E, Bernal-Sprekelsen M, Serpelloni G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Trimarchi M, Landis BN, Simmen D, Saleh H, East C, Herman P, Bussi M, Robotti E, Bernal-Sprekelsen M, Serpelloni G, et al.
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10718-7
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900207



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cocaine-induced midline destructive lesions (CIMDL) may cause progressive septonasal and palatal destruction, but the optimal timing of reconstruction remains undefined. Because relapse is common, particularly within the first year, premature surgery may lead to failure and, in advanced cases, severe complications. This work synthesizes the available evidence and expert opinion to guide surgical timing and practical management. METHODS: We performed a narrative evidence-based review of studies addressing cocaine relapse, abstinence verification, and reconstructive or prosthetic management in CIMDL, integrated with multidisciplinary expert consensus. Key relapse data were drawn from large longitudinal cohorts, including national treatment and follow-up studies and analyses of continuing care and initial abstinence. RESULTS: Relapse risk remains clinically significant throughout the first 12 months after treatment, with weekly-use relapse rates of approximately 20-24% at 12 months. Beyond 12 months, increases appear smaller in longitudinal cohorts. Early sustained abstinence is protective, with at least 12 weeks of abstinence during treatment associated with substantially lower relapse rates. As self-report is often unreliable, repeated toxicology testing combined with serial endoscopic assessment offers objective monitoring, facilitates shared review with patients, and may improve adherence. Reconstructions beyond simple septal perforations are usually staged, and relapse during treatment can irreversibly compromise outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Based on relapse dynamics and expert consensus, reconstruction in CIMDL should be deferred until at least 12 months of toxicology-verified abstinence within a multidisciplinary pathway including structured monitoring, optimized prosthetic care, staged surgery, and prolonged postoperative surveillance.

item.title: Riedel thyroiditis mimicking malignancy: a fatal surgical outcome.
item.dc:creator: Gündoğdu Y, Çavlan CE, Tereci Oran B, Asya O, Çeşmecioğlu Karavin E, Türköz K, Yumuşakhuylu AC
item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900205



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Riedel thyroiditis (RT) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder that can mimic malignancy clinically and radiologically. We report an unusually extensive, ultimately fatal case and highlight its diagnostic and therapeutic lessons. METHODS: Case report of a 40-year-old man, with review of the clinical, imaging, histopathological and follow-up data, reported in accordance with the CARE guidelines. RESULTS: The patient presented with a right cervicothoracic mass (64 × 45 × 115 mm) circumferentially encasing the common carotid, subclavian and innominate vessels with mediastinal extension. Three tissue procedures were non-diagnostic and FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 8.15). Radical en bloc resection was undertaken because malignancy could not be excluded. The course was complicated by bilateral vocal-cord paralysis, Horner syndrome, mediastinitis, osteomyelitis and a tracheo-innominate fistula. Histology showed obliterative phlebitis, storiform fibrosis and 74 IgG4-positive plasma cells/HPF (IgG4:IgG 44%), confirming RT despite normal serum IgG4. The patient died of a recurrent tracheo-innominate fistula approximately 20 months postoperatively. CONCLUSION: RT can mimic malignancy and, when radical surgery is undertaken for diagnostic uncertainty, may prove fatal. Adequate tissue sampling with IgG4 immunostaining is essential before contemplating radical surgery.

item.title: Stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (sTIL) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma: association with pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, and mortality.
item.dc:creator: Erol S, Büyük BB, Erol A, Bozdoğan N, Toprak F, Arslan A
item.description:
Authors: Erol S, Büyük BB, Erol A, Bozdoğan N, Toprak F, Arslan A
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10680-4
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900202



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Previous studies suggest a favorable prognostic role for tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, although findings vary by immune-cell phenotype, assessment method, tumor compartment, and cohort characteristics. This study evaluated associations between sTIL percentage and pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, and mortality after surgery. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 81 patients who underwent primary or salvage total laryngectomy between January 2019 and March 2024. sTIL was assessed on H&E sections according to International TILs Working Group guidelines. Because sTIL was non-normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk W = 0.908; p < 0.001), non-parametric tests were used. Associations were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, and Spearman correlation. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Median sTIL was 30% (IQR: 10-50%). sTIL was not significantly associated with fistula, recurrence, mortality, surgical approach, lymphovascular or perineural invasion, T stage, or differentiation grade (all p > 0.05). Mortality was associated with older age (68 vs. 60 years; p = 0.004). Deceased patients had longer observed follow-up, reflecting time-to-event structure rather than a prognostic association. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no survival difference by sTIL group (log-rank p = 0.914). CONCLUSIONS: H&E-based sTIL scoring was not significantly associated with pharyngocutaneous fistula, recurrence, or overall survival. Given the limited number of fistula events, the fistula-related findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Age and lymphovascular invasion were independently associated with mortality. These non-confirmatory findings require validation in larger studies using spatial and phenotypic immune profiling.

item.title: Association of beta-blockers use with risk and clinical outcomes of head and neck cancer: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Zhang LE, Aizawa Y, Oishi A, Kanai S, Sumita Y, Hirai H, Tomihara K
item.description:
Authors: Zhang LE, Aizawa Y, Oishi A, Kanai S, Sumita Y, Hirai H, Tomihara K
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10685-z
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42900201



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Preclinical evidence suggests beta-blockers (BBs) may inhibit stress-induced tumor progression, but clinical data on their association with head and neck cancer (HNC) outcomes remain conflicting. This study evaluated the association between BB use and the risk and prognosis of HNC. METHODS: A comprehensive search of five databases was conducted. We performed a meta-analysis to assess cancer risk, overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) between BB users and non-users. Heterogeneity was explored by subgroup and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Seven studies were included. BB use was significantly associated with a reduced risk of HNC (RR = 0.58, 95%CI: 0.45-0.75). But in patients with HNC, BB use was linked to poor prognostic outcomes. Users demonstrated significantly worse DFS (HR = 1.85, 95%CI: 1.10-3.11) and DSS (HR = 1.82, 95%CI: 1.39-2.39). Exploratory subgroup analysis identified that cancer type might be a potential source of heterogeneity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest a potential inverse association between BB use and the development of HNC. This estimate should be regarded as exploratory because it is derived from only two eligible non-lip head and neck cancer cohorts. In diagnosed patients, observational data link BB use to poorer DFS and DSS. However, given the statistical fragility of these prognostic estimates and potential confounding by indication, these trends must be interpreted with caution. Current evidence does not support BBs as adjuvant therapy for HNC. Future studies should prioritize adjustment for comorbidities and stratification by HPV status and tumor subsite.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Quantitative pathological lymph node parameters (qpLNP), i.e. lymph node yield (LNY), lymph node ratio (LNR), and weighted lymph node ratio (WLNR), are potential prognostic markers in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Incorporation into post-operative staging may help to direct more precise adjuvant treatment regimens. Available data warrant more detailed subgroup analyses, we therefore evaluated their prognostic value with particular attention to neck dissection laterality, pN0 disease, and patients without recommendation for adjuvant therapy. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of 410 surgically treated HNSCC patients from a single tertiary center (2010-2020). Data-derived cutoffs were determined by recursive partitioning. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, log-rank tests, and multivariable Cox regression. 67 patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma were analyzed separately. RESULTS: In 343 patients with HPV-unrelated HNSCC, LNY, LNR, and WLNR were independently associated with overall survival on multivariable analysis (LNY: HR 1.58, p=0.012; LNR: HR 1.77, p=0.026; WLNR: HR 2.30, p<0.001). Discriminative performance increased from LNY (C-index 0.55) to LNR (0.59) to WLNR (0.61). Prognostic signal was primarily driven by the ipsilateral and not the contralateral neck. LNY (HR 1.92, p=0.044) and WLNR (HR 2.31, p=0.038) showed prognostic value in patients without adjuvant therapy, and LNY remained independently prognostic in node-negative patients on multivariable analysis (HR 1.88, p=0.027). Site-specific analyses in patients with HPV-unrelated oropharyngeal carcinoma and oral cavity carcinoma treated with bilateral neck dissection confirmed independent prognostic value for LNY and WLNR in both subgroups. In HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma, qpLNP held no prognostic value. Here, extranodal extension was the dominant prognostic factor. CONCLUSION: LNY, LNR, and WLNR provide complementary prognostic information in HPV-unrelated HNSCC. The validity of LNY in node-negative patients emphasizes its value as a quality control parameter for surgery while WLNR's performance in patients without adjuvant therapy suggests additional value in patient stratification for adjuvant treatment.

item.title: Activity of Low Dose Nivolumab in Patients With Advanced Squamous Cell Carcinomas and Other Cancers.

Abstract:
Immune checkpoint inhibitors such as anti-PD-1 antibodies are essential in cancer therapy. Emerging data suggest that lower doses may be effective and more economical, though further evidence is needed. We conducted a retrospective study at Centre Léon Bérard to assess the efficacy and safety of low-dose nivolumab (20 mg every 3 weeks) in patients with advanced cancer, mainly squamous cell carcinomas (SCC). Between 2023 and 2024, 53 patients were treated, with a median age of 74 years; 39.6% were over 80. Most were male (64%) and had ECOG ≥ 2 (69.9%). Primary tumor sites included cutaneous SCC (34%), head and neck SCC (32%), and soft tissue sarcoma (15%). After a median follow-up of 8.3 months, median overall survival was 7.5 months. The objective response rate (ORR) was 20.8%, driven by the SCC subgroup; no responses were observed in non-SCC histologies, in patients with prior ICI exposure, or beyond the second line of treatment. Among IO-naïve SCC patients treated in first or second line (n = 22), ORR was 50%. Toxicity was manageable: 18.7% experienced immune-related adverse events, with only 3.7% grade 3. item.title: Precision Thyroid Oncology Using Genetic-Based Therapies: A Narrative Review.
item.dc:creator: Marotta V, Xing M, Vitale M
item.description:
Authors: Marotta V, Xing M, Vitale M
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261497620
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42897968



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most thyroid malignancies harbor a limited set of well-characterized mutations driving tumor initiation and determining phenotype. This relatively direct genotype-phenotype association, bringing insights into molecular mechanisms of progression and drug resistance, makes advanced thyroid cancers suitable for genetic-based therapies. Personalized cancer treatment by targeting actionable tumor mutations represents one of the most innovative frontiers in oncology. SUMMARY: The present narrative review focuses on actionable mutations occurring in thyroid cancers and provides a state-of-the-art overview of genetic-based treatments that have received regulatory approval worldwide. These include two selective RET inhibitors (sRET-Is) (selpercatinib and pralsetinib), three NTRK inhibitors (NTRK-Is) (larotrectinib, entrectinib, and repotrectinib), and two dual BRAF/MEK inhibitor regimens (dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib). The most significant impact has been observed in the management of RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. Selpercatinib, available in many countries, demonstrated superiority over standard multikinase inhibitors (MKIs) in a head-to-head comparison. It currently represents the best first-line treatment option. In BRAFV600E-positive anaplastic thyroid cancer, both dabrafenib plus trametinib and encorafenib plus binimetinib showed efficacy that appeared to exceed that historically observed with standard approaches. However, their approval is currently limited to a few countries. In radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), sRET-Is and NTRK-Is are effective in molecularly selected patients and are approved in many countries. However, their applicability is limited by the low prevalence of the corresponding actionable alterations. In BRAFV600E-positive radioiodine-refractory DTC, dabrafenib plus trametinib has emerged as a useful option after MKI failure, although a tumor-specific approval has been granted only in Europe. CONCLUSIONS: Precision oncology is increasingly being integrated into the management of advanced thyroid cancer. However, its impact varies widely across different tumor settings, and its real-world use is strongly influenced by country-specific drug regulations.

item.title: Predicting drooling severity after surgery in youth with neurodevelopmental disabilities: development of a proof-of-principle multivariable prognostic model.
item.dc:creator: van den Nieuwenhof DWA, Donders R, van Hulst K, Orriëns LB, Erasmus CE, van den Hoogen FJA, Bekkers S
item.description:
Authors: van den Nieuwenhof DWA, Donders R, van Hulst K, Orriëns LB, Erasmus CE, van den Hoogen FJA, Bekkers S
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104965
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42913180



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Predicting outcomes of surgery for drooling could support candidate selection and shape expectations for patients and caregivers. This study describes the development of a prognostic prediction model for the expected drooling Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at 32-weeks post-surgery in youth with a neurodevelopmental disability. METHODS: A multivariable linear model was developed with data from a prospectively gathered pseudonymized database of drooling patients from the Saliva Control Clinic of a Dutch tertiary care center. The population consisted of drooling patients with a non-progressive neurodevelopmental disability who underwent surgery for drooling between January 2000 and March 2023. The outcome measure for the model was the VAS at 32-week follow-up. The baseline VAS was incorporated in the model to take into account the relative change compared to baseline. Internal validation was performed using bootstrapping. RESULTS: The model was developed based on 227 patients (37.4% female, median age at surgery = 14.0). The final parsimonious model included 15 variables, resulting in an apparent pooled R2 = 0.26 and an R2-adjusted= 0.21. Internal validation resulted in a calibration slope of 0.86 with an optimism-corrected R2 of 0.16. Several parameters contributed significantly to predicting the outcome after surgery. These included age, VAS at baseline, type of surgery, type of neurodevelopmental disability, ambulatory status, use of laxatives or prokinetic agents, severe dysphagia, and abnormal oral suction and propulsion capacity. DISCUSSION: This study provides a proof of principle that a multivariable linear prediction model can estimate postoperative anterior drooling severity in youth with neurodevelopmental disabilities undergoing surgery, using routinely available clinical characteristics. The model has not undergone external validation and is therefore not intended for clinical use in its current form. Rather, these findings demonstrate the potential of individualized outcome prediction in this population and support multicenter collaboration for external validation and further refinement. If validated, such a model could eventually support clinicians and caregivers in setting realistic expectations and assessing whether the anticipated benefit of an already selected surgical procedure is sufficient to proceed with surgery.

item.title: Long-term efficacy, clinical outcomes, and safety of vimseltinib in patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumor: results from the MOTION phase 3 trial.
item.dc:creator: Bhadri V, Gelderblom H, Stacchiotti S, Bauer S, Wagner AJ, van de Sande M, Bernthal NM, López Pousa A, Abdul Razak A, Italiano A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bhadri V, Gelderblom H, Stacchiotti S, Bauer S, Wagner AJ, van de Sande M, Bernthal NM, López Pousa A, Abdul Razak A, Italiano A, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag421
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42898002



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) is a locally aggressive neoplasm caused by colony-stimulating factor 1 (CSF1) gene dysregulation. Vimseltinib is an oral, switch-control tyrosine kinase inhibitor of the CSF1 receptor. In part 1 of the MOTION phase 3 trial, vimseltinib demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in antitumor activity and clinical outcome assessments (COAs). Here, we report long-term results from MOTION in patients with >2 years of follow-up on study. PATIENTS AND METHODS: MOTION is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial with double-blind (part 1; to week 25), open-label (part 2; weeks 25-49), and extension periods (NCT05059262). Eligible adult patients with histologically confirmed TGCT not amenable to surgery received vimseltinib 30 mg twice weekly. Efficacy was assessed by objective response rate (ORR) on study evaluated by independent radiological review per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1) and Tumor Volume Score. COAs and safety were assessed. RESULTS: In total, 118 patients received vimseltinib during MOTION (randomized to vimseltinib, n = 83; crossover, n = 35), with 51% (60/118) remaining on treatment. ORR on study per RECIST v1.1 was 48% (40/83) for patients randomized to vimseltinib and 54% (19/35) for crossover. Patients in both groups experienced long-term improvements in COAs. The safety profile was consistent with prior reports, with no evidence of cholestatic hepatotoxicity or drug-induced liver injury. CONCLUSION: Vimseltinib continued to provide robust and durable antitumor activity and demonstrated long-term improvements in COAs, with manageable safety for the treatment of patients with TGCT not amenable to surgery.

item.title: Association Between Oral Health Status at Admission and Length of Hospital Stay in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study (2024-2025).
item.dc:creator: San Martín Harms MV, Mujica Valenzuela I, Fischer Prato D, Prieto D, Coloma Osorio MC, Roldán Sánchez L, Regueira T, Ortuño D
item.description:
Authors: San Martín Harms MV, Mujica Valenzuela I, Fischer Prato D, Prieto D, Coloma Osorio MC, Roldán Sánchez L, Regueira T, Ortuño D

Published: 2026-Oct-19

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor oral health is linked to prolonged hospitalization, but critical care data from Latin America remain virtually absent. This study characterized baseline oral health at intensive care unit (ICU) admission in a Chilean center and evaluated its association with ICU length of stay (LOS). METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including first-admission adults (n = 105). Bedside clinical examinations at admission assessed the WHO Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index, gingival inflammation, and salivary hypofunction. Adjusted associations with ICU LOS were evaluated using multivariable ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. RESULTS: At admission, gingival inflammation and salivary hypofunction were each present in 90.5% of patients. The mean DMFT was 8.87 ± 9.40. In multivariable analysis, the DMFT index was not associated with ICU LOS (β = -0.050, 95% CI [-0.187, 0.087], p = 0.477). Mechanical ventilation status emerged as the sole independent predictor of prolonged stay (β = 3.30 days, 95% CI [0.75, 5.85], p = 0.013). Results were robust across five sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Despite a remarkably high baseline burden of oral disease at ICU admission, chronic caries experience was not independently associated with ICU LOS, which was driven primarily by ventilatory support.

item.title: The Association Between Oral Lichen Planus and Diabetes Mellitus: A Scoping Review of the Evidence.
item.dc:creator: Alamoudi W
item.description:
Authors: Alamoudi W
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70552
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42897782



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated oral potentially malignant disorder. Three prior meta-analyses reported elevated diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence in patients with OLP, but the evidence base has since expanded. This scoping review synthesised all available evidence on the OLP-DM association up to November 2025. STUDY DESIGN: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to November 30, 2025 with no lower date limit, supplemented by backward citation searching. No study design restrictions were applied. Findings were synthesised thematically per PRISMA-ScR. RESULTS: Twenty-one sources from 11 countries were included, encompassing observational studies, Mendelian randomisation analyses, biochemical investigations, reviews, and case reports. DM prevalence in patients with OLP ranged from 9.7% to 24.5%, with the association specific to type 2 DM. Prediabetes was independently associated with OLP after multivariate adjustment. Mendelian randomisation provided causal evidence linking type 1 DM and elevated glycated haemoglobin to increased OLP risk. CONCLUSIONS: The OLP-DM association is consistent, biologically plausible, and extends to subclinical glycaemic dysregulation. Glycaemic assessment should be considered in patients with OLP presenting with oral or systemic features suggestive of metabolic dysregulation. Future research should prioritise longitudinal studies, intervention trials on glycaemic optimisation.

item.title: Association Between Oxidative Stress Biomarkers and Periodontitis in Saliva and Gingival Crevicular Fluid: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Fan ZX, Wang XY, Liu C, Yang J
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70542
Published: 2026-Oct-19

Abstract:
AIM: This systematic review aimed to synthesize current observational evidence on the association between oxidative stress (OS) biomarker levels in saliva and gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and periodontitis. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from 2000 to 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa and percent agreement. Publication bias was investigated using Egger's test. RESULTS: Out of 1695 records, 31 prospective studies and 54 cross-sectional studies met the inclusion criteria. In the primary analyses, periodontitis was associated with higher total oxidant status (TOS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and 8-hydroxy-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) levels and lower total antioxidant capacity (TAC) in both saliva and GCF. In GCF, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione (GSH) levels were lower, whereas glutathione peroxidase (GPX) was higher. No significant differences were found for salivary SOD, GSH, GPX, or glutathione reductase (GR) in the primary analyses. However, after trim-and-fill adjustment, the initially significant salivary TAC and 8-OHdG associations were no longer statistically significant. Substantial heterogeneity was observed among evaluated studies. CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis supports an association between periodontitis and altered OS biomarker levels in saliva and GCF. item.title: Evaluation of the Clinical Efficacy of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in the Treatment of Oral Leukoplakia.

Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70497
Published: 2026-Oct-19

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) in treating oral leukoplakia (OLK), thereby exploring a novel therapeutic approach for this condition. METHODS: 17 OLK patients treated at the Department of Oral Mucosal Diseases between June 2022 and February 2023 underwent HIFU therapy. Postoperative clinical efficacy and adverse reactions were evaluated. RESULTS: At the 6-month follow-up, the outcomes were as follows: complete remission in 9 cases (52.95%), partial remission in 6 cases (35.29%), no remission in 2 cases (11.76%). The overall response rate reached 88.24%. 2 h postoperatively, 2 patients experienced significant pain, while the remaining patients reported mild pain (VAS score: 0.88 ± 1.83, M = 0). Patients with cheeks or commissural leukoplakia showed no swelling. Except for 1 case, patients with dorsal tongue leukoplakia exhibited mild swelling that resolved spontaneously within 2 ~ 24 h. Between 24 and 72 h postoperatively, all 16 patients except one developed noticeable ulcers with mild pain (VAS score: 1.1 ± 0.84, M = 1), which healed within 2-3 weeks. CONCLUSION: HIFU demonstrates significant clinical efficacy in treating OLK. Postoperative reactions are localized and well-tolerated, markedly improving patients' quality of life.

item.title: Differential Diagnosis Performance of ChatGPT in Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology.
item.dc:creator: Shujaat S, Riaz M, Alsubaie JM, Almuammar AA, Pillai A, Alfadley A, Aboalela AA
item.description:

Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70501
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42897769



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) for ranked differential diagnoses in oral and maxillofacial pathology, assess image effects on diagnostic performance and examine output stability across repeated runs. METHODS: This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 160 biopsy-confirmed cases. Cases were evaluated using a standardised prompt under two conditions: text-only and text plus clinical photographs and/or radiographs. Each case underwent three independent runs. Performance was measured using Top-1, Top-3, Top-5 and Top-10 accuracy. RESULTS: Top-1 accuracy was 44.0% for text-only and 43.3% for text + image inputs. Accuracy increased at broader thresholds, with Top-10 accuracy reaching 80.7% and 82.9%, respectively, but no significant differences were observed between input conditions at any Top-K threshold. Top-1 performance was stable across runs, although variability was observed at broader Top-K thresholds in the text-only condition. CONCLUSIONS: ChatGPT ranked the reference diagnosis first in fewer than half of cases, while broader differential lists more often included it. Images did not significantly improve accuracy, although heterogeneous and non-standardised visual inputs may have limited detection of multimodal effects. These findings support further investigation for hypothesis generation and educational use rather than clinical decision support or replacement of expert judgement and histopathological confirmation.

item.title: Effect of Pilocarpine on Salivary Flow Rate in Patients With Xerostomia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

Published: 2026-Oct-19

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Xerostomia is a common clinical condition that significantly impairs oral health and quality of life. Pilocarpine, a muscarinic agonist, is frequently prescribed to stimulate salivary secretion. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. Electronic searches of PubMed, Cochrane Library, Science Direct, Scopus, Embase and Google Scholar were performed for randomized controlled trials published between January 2005 and November 2025. Trials comparing pilocarpine with placebo in patients with xerostomia confirmed by sialometry were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB) 2.0 tool. Meta-analysis was performed using StataCorp software 2025 with standardized mean differences of salivary flow rate. RESULTS: 12 randomized controlled trials involving 599 participants were included, with 7 studies contributing to the meta-analysis. Pilocarpine showed a statistically significant improvement in salivary flow rate compared with placebo (SMD = 0.15; 95% CI: 0.06-0.25; p < 0.001; I2 = 98%). Subgroup analysis demonstrated a significant effect for topical pilocarpine (I2 = 72%), while systemic pilocarpine did not show statistical significance (I2 = 96%). CONCLUSIONS: Pilocarpine improves salivary flow rate in patients with xerostomia, particularly when residual salivary gland function is preserved, with topical formulations showing more consistent evidence of efficacy. However, given the high heterogeneity, results should be interpreted cautiously.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to better understand the expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 proteins in progressive and nonprogressive oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) cell lines to predict malignant transformation. RESULTS: CDKN2A and NOTCH1 had low expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0008 and 0.0012) respectively relative to nonprogressive OED, indicating a negative tendency. CONCLUSION: The current study illustrates that the high expression of p53, combined with low expression of CDKN2A and NOTCH1, may serve as helpful markers, providing a potential molecular complement to histopathology for predicting malignant transformation in OED.

item.title: The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Oral Cancer Screening: Real-World Data From Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Kao YH, Lin MN, Yao WL, Huang YT, Wang WC, Yang YW, Ho PS
item.description:
Authors: Kao YH, Lin MN, Yao WL, Huang YT, Wang WC, Yang YW, Ho PS
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70547
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42897759



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening services worldwide, but its impact across multiple screening indicators remains unclear. METHODS: This population-based interrupted time series study evaluated the impact of COVID-19 on oral cancer screening in Taiwan. Two intervention points were defined: January 2020 and May 2021. Four indicators were assessed: screening rate, screening positivity rate, incidence, and mortality. Segmented regression analyses were performed across six National Health Insurance divisions, and changes in stage at diagnosis (2018-2022) were examined. RESULTS: At baseline, screening rates declined, screening positivity rate and mortality increased modestly, and incidence remained stable. After the first outbreak, screening positivity rate showed a significant immediate decrease (OR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92, p < 0.001), whereas screening rate, incidence, and mortality showed no significant changes. Advanced-stage diagnoses increased, while early-stage diagnoses declined. Regional analyses demonstrated similar patterns. No significant slope changes after the first outbreak or level/trend changes after the second outbreak were observed. Incidence and mortality remained stable throughout the study. CONCLUSIONS: The first outbreak had the greatest impact on screening-related indicators, with findings consistent with possible delays in cancer detection. Maintaining organized screening services during public health emergencies is essential to minimize delayed cancer detection.

item.title: Clinicoepidemiologic Profile of Oral Kaposi Sarcoma in People Living With HIV: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To characterize the clinicoepidemiologic profile of HIV-associated oral Kaposi sarcoma (OKS) and quantitatively synthesize its frequency, anatomical distribution, and temporal patterns across antiretroviral therapy (ART) eras. METHODS: Six databases and gray literature were searched. Eligible observational, descriptive, and quasi-experimental studies were appraised using JBI tools. Random-effects meta-analyses of patient-based proportions and treatment-era subgroup were performed when compatible study-level denominators were available (PROSPERO: CRD420251105061). RESULTS: Forty-eight studies comprising 1661 individuals were included, and 31 contributed to at least one meta-analysis. Pooled proportions were 0.85 (95% CI: 0.76-0.91) for palatal involvement and 0.44 (95% CI: 0.23-0.68) for OKS as a sentinel presentation of HIV. Pooled prevalence of OKS among people living with HIV was 0.06 (95% CI: 0.02-0.12). Compared with the pre-combination ART era, the combination ART era showed lower palatal (0.72 vs. 0.89; p = 0.0034) and gingival involvement (0.07 vs. 0.30; p = 0.0003), but more sentinel presentations (0.72 vs. 0.32; p = 0.0195). Temporal subgroup findings suggest changes in oral distribution across ART eras while reinforcing its persistent role as a sentinel manifestation of HIV infection and persistent clinical relevance despite ART.

item.title: The double jeopardy effect of socioeconomic barriers on guideline-concordant postoperative radiation in oropharyngeal cancer.

Abstract:
Receipt of timely adjuvant radiation after primary surgery for head and neck cancer is a well-established quality benchmark.
