Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is increasing in several Western countries, but this trend is less well understood in other geographical regions and for other head and neck cancers (HNC). The BROADEN (absolute BuRden Of HPV relAteD hEad and Neck) study assessed HPV-attributable fractions (HPV-AFs) of HNC including OPC in France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, China, and Japan over a 10-year period. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with HNC (oropharynx, oral cavity, nasopharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx cancer) in two time periods, 2008-2009 and 2018-2019. Formalin-fixed tissue samples were centrally tested for HPV-DNA, HPV-E6*I mRNA, and p16INK4a immunohistochemistry. HPV attributability required positive results in two of the three tests for OPC, and both HPV-DNA and HPV-E6*I mRNA positivity for other HNC. RESULTS: Among 6043 patients from 88 hospitals, the HPV-AF in OPC shown an increasing trend across all countries, with an HPV-AF ranging between 0% in Portugal and 44.2% in Japan in 2008-2009, and 20.0% and 51.7%, respectively, in 2018-2019. The increasing trend reached the statistical significance at 0.05 in all countries except China and Japan. Japan had the highest HPV-AF in 2008-2009. Other HNC showed lower HPV-AF (≤5%) with no time trends. CONCLUSION: BROADEN is the first and largest study to date to investigate HPV causality and its time trends across five HNCs in seven countries. These results support the understanding of time trends and geographic variation in HPV-AF and are essential for global HNC prevention and treatment.

item.title: Phosphorylation of IRS4 at YY111/112 promotes LUSC progression via PI3K/AKT pathway activation.
item.dc:creator: Aihemaiti Y, Ren Q, Jiang X, Wushaying K, Chen R, Wang Y, Zhao X, Xu L, Yang Z, Yu J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Aihemaiti Y, Ren Q, Jiang X, Wushaying K, Chen R, Wang Y, Zhao X, Xu L, Yang Z, Yu J, et al.
Journal: Oncogene | DOI: 10.1038/s41388-026-04015-0
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 42892654



Abstract:
Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) lacks effective targeted therapies despite frequent hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, and the contribution of adaptor proteins to this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify Insulin Receptor Substrate 4 (IRS4) as a common substrate of Src kinase and the phosphatase RPTPα, and uncover a previously unrecognized, conserved phosphorylation site at YY111/112 within the IRS4 PH domain. Src-mediated phosphorylation at this site is essential for IRS4-driven proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, and invasiveness in LUSC cells. Mechanistically, phosphorylation at YY111/112 induces conformational rearrangements in IRS4 that enhance the recruitment of the p85β SH2 domain to the YXXM motif of IRS4, thereby promoting AKT activation without altering IRS4 protein stability or subcellular distribution. An IRS4-derived cell-permeable phosphopeptide containing pYY111/112 disrupts the Src-IRS4 interaction and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo in a YY111/112-dependent manner. Consistently, YY111/112 phosphorylation is markedly elevated in human LUSC tissues and correlates with advanced disease stages. Collectively, these findings define a Src-IRS4-PI3K/AKT signaling axis and identify YY111/112 as a critical regulatory site of IRS4 and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUSC.

item.title: Machine learning-based prediction of malignant transformation within 5 years in patients with oral leukoplakia: A retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Yang Q, Zhou M, Zhang C, Lu Y, Lan Q, Wei P, Hua H
item.description:
Authors: Yang Q, Zhou M, Zhang C, Lu Y, Lan Q, Wei P, Hua H
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108174
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 42892164



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral leukoplakia (OLK), a potentially malignant oral disorder, has 7.2 - 9.8 % transformation rate. Identifying high-risk patients within 5 years can reduce the oral cancer burden. OBJECTIVE: In this retrospective study, we aimed to identify the factors associated with malignant transformation in Chinese patients with OLK and develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models for predicting malignant transformation within 5 years. METHODS: In total, 672 OLK patients (203 showing transformation; 469 with no transformation) were included. Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, GBDT, XGBoost, and LightGBM ML algorithms were used to develop models based on 17 clinicopathological features and evaluated using an internal test set and a temporal validation cohort of 73 patients (24 showing transformation; 49 with no transformation). RESULTS: LightGBM showed the best overall performance in the internal test set (accuracy, 82.65 %; area under the curve (AUC), 0.8524), and it maintained good discriminative performance in the temporal validation cohort (AUC, 0.7959) when 17 clinicopathological features were used. XGBoost showed the best performance in both the internal test set (AUC, 0.8081) and temporal validation cohort (AUC, 0.8092) when five clinicopathological features were used. While predicting malignant transformation within 5 years, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.8505 in the internal test set. However, the temporal validation results should be interpreted with caution because of limited sample size. CONCLUSION: ML models may predict malignant transformation within 5 years in patients with OLK and may assist in individualized risk stratification. Further validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical application.

item.title: Distinct epigenetic signatures define HPV-positive and HPV-negative tonsil carcinomas.
item.dc:creator: van der Heijden M, Kommer M, Boers JB, van den Munckhof HAM, Hardillo JA, van Kemenade FJ, de Jong RJB, Boers RG, Keereweer S
item.description:
Authors: van der Heijden M, Kommer M, Boers JB, van den Munckhof HAM, Hardillo JA, van Kemenade FJ, de Jong RJB, Boers RG, Keereweer S
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108186
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 42892163



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Epigenetic modifications, particularly DNA methylation, play a key role in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). This is the first study to apply genome-wide methylated DNA sequencing (MeD-seq) to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) in OPSCC. By comparing HPV-positive and HPV-negative tonsillar carcinomas, we evaluate MeD-seq's applicability to validate known and identify novel DMRs. These findings may support the identification of potential biomarkers for risk stratification and prognostic assessment in OPSCC. METHODS: Methylated DNA sequencing (MeD-seq) was used to analyze genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tonsil samples. Gene set enrichment analysis explored the biological role of DMR associated genes. A literature search of DMR's was performed to compare MeD-seq to other techniques. RESULTS: Thirty-one analyzed samples (10 HPV + OPSCC, 9 HPV- OPSCC, and 12 controls) revealed 4,962 DMRs. We focused on the top five promoter-region DMRs with the highest fold change per comparison (HPV + vs. HPV-; HPV + vs. controls; HPV - vs. controls). Key DMRs involved IRF4, TCF24, and CLSTN2. IRF4 was hypermethylated in both OPSCC groups compared to controls, while CLSTN2 was hypermethylated in HPV + versus HPV - tumors. Enrichment analysis indicated enrichment of cell cycle-related pathways in HPV + tumors and IGF1R signaling pathways in HPV - tumors. MeD-seq confirmed known methylation patterns and identified novel OPSCC-specific DMRs. DISCUSSION: This pilot study demonstrates HPV-associated methylation profiles in OPSCC, highlighting MeD-seq as a reliable technique for tumor methylation analysis, confirming existing and identifying novel DMRs. Larger studies are needed to validate potential biomarkers for prognosis and personalized treatment.

item.title: Accuracy of Diagnostic Methods for Peripheral Trigeminal Nerve Injuries: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Varvara G, Burdo P, Gerardi D, Lozza A, Biglioli F
item.description:
Authors: Varvara G, Burdo P, Gerardi D, Lozza A, Biglioli F
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.006
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42913723



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy following oral and maxillofacial procedures may cause persistent neurosensory disturbances and neuropathic pain, yet the diagnostic performance of the available assessment methods remains uncertain. PURPOSE: This systematic review evaluated the accuracy of diagnostic methods used to detect peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries in the maxillary and mandibular regions after oral and maxillofacial procedures. STUDY SELECTION: PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Diagnostic accuracy and observational studies evaluating clinical, neurophysiological, or imaging-based methods for peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries were included, while non-English and nonhuman studies, reports lacking relevant diagnostic performance data, studies outside the maxillary or mandibular regions, and nonoriginal research were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2. RESULTS: The search identified 2914 records, of which 10 studies (0.3%) were included in the final synthesis, comprising n = 520 participants and k = 514 injured or evaluated nerves. The included studies comprised 5 prospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 retrospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 case-control diagnostic accuracy studies, and one cross-sectional observational study. Clinical neurosensory testing showed 96% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, 62.5% specificity, 95% positive predictive value (PPV), and 100% negative predictive value (NPV) for lingual nerve (LN) injuries, compared with 73% accuracy, 85% sensitivity, 47% specificity, 77% PPV, and 60% NPV for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. The tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic field laterality index showed 95.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 90.9% NPV for LN injury. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Clinical neurosensory testing was widely used but had variable diagnostic performance, with lower values for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. Quantitative sensory testing and neurophysiological methods provided more balanced diagnostic profiles, especially when combined. Magnetic resonance neurography demonstrated high specificity but variable sensitivity, with greater clinical value for high-fgrade injuries. The highest single-test accuracy was reported for tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic fields in LN injury. Overall, these findings support a multimodal diagnostic approach when objective confirmation, injury grading, anatomical localization, or treatment planning is required.

item.title: An R-loop-related gene signature predicts prognosis and shapes the immune microenvironment in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Meng C, Su H, Yan R, Sun R, Yu Q, Meng Y, Xi Y
item.description:
Authors: Meng C, Su H, Yan R, Sun R, Yu Q, Meng Y, Xi Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16564-4
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42926202



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) features a poor prognosis and unclear pathogenesis, and the role of R-loops, key regulators of genome stability, has not been systematically characterized in this disease. METHODS: Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data of ESCC were integrated with published R-loop-related genes (RLRGs) to construct an RLRG scoring system. The associations between the RLRG score and prognosis, tumor immune microenvironment, and tumor stemness were analyzed via multiple bioinformatics algorithms. The expression of core genes was verified using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western Blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Seven key RLRGs related to the prognosis of the ESCC patients were identified, among which three core genes-BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155-were significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues compared with controls, as confirmed by both bioinformatic analysis and experimental validation. Notably, BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155 were co-enriched in DNA replication, pyrimidine metabolism, RNA degradation, and MYC target pathways, which are closely linked to R-loop biology and suggest potential crosstalk between these genes and R-loop regulatory networks. Meanwhile, the low RLRGs score group exhibited significantly worse overall survival but displayed a more active yet dysfunctional immune microenvironment. Single-cell analysis identified SquamousEpithelium cells as the key cell type with the highest RLRG scores across five independent algorithms. Malignant SquamousEpithelium cells with high RLRG scores showed enhanced stemness and activation of pathways including JAK-STAT, hypoxia, and DNA repair. CONCLUSION: This study provided the first systematic characterization of the R-loop landscape in ESCC, suggests that SquamousEpithelium cells may play a key role in R-loop-associated progression and are identified as potential prognostic biomarkers with possible therapeutic relevance that requires functional validation.

item.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Mandibular and Maxillary Fracture Research: Global Trends and Paradigm Shifts From 2005 to 2026.
item.dc:creator: Sakamoto Y, Kojima Y, Tsukimoto S, Sanuki T, Miura K
item.description:
Authors: Sakamoto Y, Kojima Y, Tsukimoto S, Sanuki T, Miura K
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.002
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42925885



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of mandibular and maxillary fractures is undergoing a transition from conventional open reduction and internal fixation toward precision surgery driven by three-dimensional printing, computer-assisted navigation, and artificial intelligence. While traditional citation counts reflect past academic impact, they do not necessarily capture the current cutting edge. Bibliometric analysis has therefore gained attention as an objective approach to visualize paradigm shifts and emerging research frontiers. PURPOSE: This study aimed to perform a bibliometric analysis of original articles on mandibular and maxillary fractures published over the past 2 decades, in order to clarify citation accumulation, the evolution of research topics, major contributing countries, and emerging digital trends. STUDY SELECTION: A title-based search of the Scopus database was conducted on May 10, 2026, for English-language original articles published from 2005 to 2026. The query combined fracture-related terms ("mandibular," "maxillary," "condylar," "subcondylar," "TMJ," and "Le Fort") with treatment-related terms ("fixation," "osteosynthesis," "management," "surgical," and "treatment"). The exclusion criteria comprised animal experiments, in vitro studies, case reports, elective orthognathic procedures without trauma context, oncological reconstructions, and routine implantology studies. Of the 1,168 articles initially retrieved, 842 (72.1%) met the inclusion criteria. RESULTS: The mean annual growth rate of publications was 0.99% (simple annual average), with a marked acceleration after 2020. The total number of citations was 31,577 (mean: 12.94 per article). India, China, and the United States ranked highest among corresponding author countries (used as a proxy for national contribution), and the international coauthorship rate was 11.4%. From 2006 to 2012, dominant topics concerned fixation materials and open reduction techniques, whereas keywords such as "three-dimensional printing," "computed tomography," and "navigation" emerged rapidly after 2020, with 3D printing showing the highest citation impact among emerging digital keywords. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This bibliometric analysis suggests that published research on mandibular and maxillary fracture management has increasingly focused on digitally assisted workflows in recent years. These findings indicate a shift in research attention rather than proven clinical superiority of newer technologies and may help clarify priorities for future research in oral and maxillofacial trauma.

item.title: Genesis-progression of early jaw osteoradionecrosis in head and neck cancer survivors: dynamics of independent but interconnected factors.
item.dc:creator: Delanian SE
item.description:
Authors: Delanian SE
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1941783
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42920861



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term head and neck cancer survivors are few, but always exposed to a risk of mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) despite the use of appropriate dose-volume constraints in today's radiotherapy. Here, ORN development is approached from another look, in an attempt to explain its complexity. DEFINITIONS: Early ORN is best defined by length of the mucosal defect (<2 teeth long) and radiological assessment of the depth of areas of bone resorption (lysis below the level of the inferior alveolar canal) in the radiotherapy volume. Technical improvements have greatly reduced the incidence of ORN, but a lifelong risk remains and requires long-term follow-up. CAUSAL FACTORS: Pathogenic hypotheses have evolved over time from the "radiation-trauma-infection" triad to the 3H theory of "hypoxia-hypocellularity-hypovascularity", and then radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone. ORN is a dynamic process combining interacting causal factors that worsen each other over time: (a) radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone and its related radiotherapy technical parameters; (b) periodontal disease/dental trauma and their related questions on optimal timing of pre- or post-radiotherapy extractions and how many teeth; (c) infection/oral microbiota and their related mechanically inaccessible bone sequestra (residual bacteria); (d) vascular factors from capillary network destruction to artery stenosis of irradiated branches and the carotid trunk. CONCLUSION: Symptomatic medical care focusing on comorbidity parameters and devitalized tissue removal is not sufficient to protect patients against ORN. These new insights should help to treat early ORN through concomitant control of these causal factors and best dental care.

item.title: Efficacy of endoscopic ultrasound-guided versus surgical gastrojejunostomy for malignant gastric outlet obstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Zhong F, Xiong D, Zhang H, Luo G
item.description:
Authors: Zhong F, Xiong D, Zhang H, Luo G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1943827
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42920445



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically compare the key outcomes of endoscopic ultrasound-guided gastrojejunostomy (EUS-GJ) versus surgical gastrojejunostomy (SGJ) for the palliative treatment of malignant gastric outlet obstruction (MGOO). METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA statement. Databases including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from inception to December 2025 for comparative studies of EUS-GJ and SGJ in treating MGOO. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Eight studies involving 760 patients were included. Pooled analysis showed no significant differences between EUS-GJ and SGJ in technical success (RR = 0.98, P = 0.08), clinical success (RR = 1.08, P = 0.07), obstruction recurrence (RR = 0.48, P = 0.05), or re-intervention rates (RR = 1.48, P = 0.61). However, the EUS-GJ group demonstrated significant advantages, including a shorter length of hospital stay (MD= -3.57 days, P<0.001), a quicker time to first oral intake (MD= -2.88 days, P<0.001), a shorter time to resume chemotherapy (MD= -16.05 days, P<0.001), and a lower overall adverse events rate (RR = 0.44, P = 0.008). CONCLUSION: For the palliative management of MGOO, EUS-GJ showed no statistically significant difference in primary efficacy endpoints compared with SGJ, but it might be associated with faster recovery and improved safety. item.title: HHLA2-KCTD12 axis: a potential mechanism regulating the biological functions of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yu Y, You J, Wang X, Xue H, Chen H, Li W
item.description:
Authors: Yu Y, You J, Wang X, Xue H, Chen H, Li W
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1898263
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42923022



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests that aberrant HHLA2 expression is closely implicated not only in tumorigenesis, disease progression, and metastatic spread, but also in the intricate modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment. Nevertheless, the biological functions of HHLA2 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its action in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain unexplored. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HHLA2 expression was systematically assessed in LSCC tumor specimens and matched adjacent tissues using multiplex immunofluorescence (mIHC). The functional consequences of HHLA2 silencing in LSCC cells were evaluated through a series of in vitro assays, including CCK-8-based proliferation analysis, wound-healing (scratch) assays, and invasion assays. Transcriptomic sequencing integrated with public database mining was subsequently performed to identify key target genes potentially governed by HHLA2 in regulating LSCC biological behavior. Furthermore, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) pathway analyses were conducted to delineate the signaling networks and molecular pathways through which HHLA2 might exert its regulatory effects in LSCC. RESULTS: HHLA2 expression was significantly elevated in LSCC tumor tissues, and associated with poor prognosis in patients. Functional experiments revealed that suppression of HHLA2 leads to marked inhibition of LSCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, underscoring its essential role in sustaining malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, we identified potassium channel tetrameric domain 12 (KCTD12) as a pivotal target of HHLA2 in mediating these oncogenic processes. Importantly, forced overexpression of KCTD12 effectively counterbalanced the inhibitory effects induced by HHLA2 depletion, thereby restoring proliferative, migratory, and invasive potential to LSCC cells. Furthermore, pathway enrichment analyses indicated that the TNF-NF-κB signalling pathway might serve as a key conduit through which HHLA2 orchestrated both tumor cell functions and immune regulatory mechanisms. The HHLA2-KCTD12 axis may regulate the phenotype of LSCC cells and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment through the TNF-NF-κB signaling pathway. CONCLUSIONS: HHLA2 enhanced the proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities of LSCC cells and might contribute to immune microenvironment remodeling via modulation of TNF-NF-κB signaling through the HHLA2-KCTD12 axis.

item.title: Calendar-defined missed-workday gaps in radiotherapy: a site- and phase-stratified audit with linkage sensitivity analyses.
item.dc:creator: Lei R, Zheng Y, Chen Y, Sun H, Qu A, Jiang P
item.description:
Authors: Lei R, Zheng Y, Chen Y, Sun H, Qu A, Jiang P
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1932765
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42908819



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Missed treatment workdays can prolong overall treatment time and may reduce tumor control, yet routine audits often conflate weekends, statutory holidays, and departmentally accepted rest schedules with untreated institutional workdays. METHODS: We quantified calendar-defined missed-workday gaps-inter-fraction intervals containing ≥1 untreated institutional workday after excluding routine rest days-among patients with first treatment between June 2021 and December 2025 who were linkable between the MOSAIQ radiotherapy information system and the institutional oncology database (1,319 patients; 1,342 episodes). A locked stratified sample of 100 algorithm-positive gaps underwent documentation-based chart review as unplanned relevant (UR) or planned/appropriate (PA). We analyzed linkage sensitivity, opportunity-adjusted site rates with patient-clustered confidence intervals (CIs), opportunity-offset Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE) including calendar year, and episode-clustered phase GEE. RESULTS: Under the documentation-based chart-review rule, 92 of 100 algorithm-positive gaps were labeled UR (17 department/equipment; 75 patient-factor) and 8 PA. Gaps occurred in 638/1,342 episodes (47.5%; patient-level 48.0%). Linked versus unlinked prevalence was 48.2% versus 51.7% (absolute difference -3.4 percentage points, 95% CI -11.2 to 4.4; P = 0.435). Among subgroups with ≥50 episodes, head and neck had the highest prevalence (75.3%) and breast the lowest (41.3%); opportunity-adjusted rates were 5.63 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 4.76-6.52) versus 2.63 (2.36-2.92) per 100 opportunities. Opportunity-offset Poisson GEE with calendar year gave a head-and-neck versus breast incidence rate ratio (IRR) of 2.99 (95% CI 2.18-4.11). An exploratory phase GEE (29,763 intervals; 1,323 clusters) showed a late versus early odds ratio (OR) of 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.54; P = 0.0009; absolute rates 2.8% vs 3.6%); after site, year, and intent adjustment, the OR was 1.32 (95% CI 1.12-1.57). CONCLUSIONS: This operational audit of institutional workdays without recorded treatment-rather than clinically confirmed unplanned interruptions-shows frequent gaps after excluding routine rest. Most reviewed positives received patient-factor labels under a documentation rule. Calendar-aware auditing may support departmental monitoring; priority-based compensation remains a proposed application.

item.title: The clinical value of ultrasound radiomics combined with clinical data nomogram in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhang X, Sun B, Jiang F, Chu Y, Wang X, Sun W, Wei T, Hong R, Ma Q
item.description:
Authors: Zhang X, Sun B, Jiang F, Chu Y, Wang X, Sun W, Wei T, Hong R, Ma Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1811434
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42908715



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. RESULTS: Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

item.title: Construction and validation of a nomogram based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators for predicting the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chen Z, Su H, Wu H, Men Q, Lv X, Zhang M, Zhang F
item.description:
Authors: Chen Z, Su H, Wu H, Men Q, Lv X, Zhang M, Zhang F
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1917420
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42908651



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between inflammation, nutrition and metabolic indicators and the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to construct and validate a nomogram for predicting PTC risk among patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgery, to assist clinicians in making more individualized clinical decisions. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective population-based cohort study. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on the clinical medical records of patients with thyroid masses who underwent surgical treatment at Hebei General Hospital from 2020 to 2024. Independent risk factors for the onset of PTC were screened through Logistic regression analysis. A risk prediction model for the onset of PTC based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators was constructed using R4.3.3 software and externally validated. RESULTS: A total of 1727 patients who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules were enrolled, among whom 1167 patients (67.6%) were pathologically-confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and 560 patients (32.4%) had benign thyroid nodules after surgery. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated combined Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) (OR = 1.887, 95%CI: 1.174-3.031, P = 0.009), combined metabolic syndrome (MetS) (OR = 2.157, 95%CI: 1.449-3.211, P < 0.001), and elevated uric acid (UA) (OR = 1.640, 95%CI: 1.112-2.417, P = 0.013) were independent risk factors for PTC onset. Age ≥ 55 years (OR = 0.318, 95%CI: 0.238-0.424, P < 0.001), other marital status (OR = 0.067, 95%CI: 0.012-0.392, P = 0.003), and increased prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR = 0.934, 95%CI: 0.902-0.966, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors against PTC onset. Based on the above independent risk factors, a nomogram for PTC was constructed. The AUC of the ROC curve in the modeling group was 0.702, and that in the external validation group was 0.721, indicating that the nomogram has good predictive performance. The calibration curve and decision analysis curve also indicate that the nomogram has good predictive performance and clinical application efficacy. CONCLUSION: Combined HT, combined MetS, and elevated UA are independent risk factors for PTC onset, whereas age ≥ 55 years, other marital status, and PNI level represent independent protective factors.

item.title: Three-Dimensional Cephalometric Analysis Based on Cone-Beam Computed Tomography of Hard and Soft Tissue Changes in Microgenia Patients Undergoing Genioplasty.
item.dc:creator: Zheng J, Ruan Y, Wang X, Liu J, Bao T
item.description:
Authors: Zheng J, Ruan Y, Wang X, Liu J, Bao T
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.09.017
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42906628



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advancement sliding genioplasty effectively corrects convex facial profiles. Characterizing hard and soft tissue changes is critical to optimizing surgical results. Cone-beam computed tomography-based three-dimensional cephalometric analysis is widely adopted to assess craniofacial surgical outcomes. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to measure the association of hard and soft tissues changes in patients with microgenia undergoing advancement sliding genioplasty. STUDY DESIGN, SAMPLE, AND SETTING: Patients with microgenia were enrolled in this retrospective cohort study from January 2024 to January 2025 at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Those with maxillofacial trauma, secondary jaw deformity, prior chin plasty, or incomplete medical notes were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor variable was microgenia severity, dichotomized based on facial convexity angle (FCA): ≤25 ° and >25 °. An FCA > 25 ° indicated more severe deformity. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLES: The primary outcome variable was soft tissue displacement relative to hard tissue displacement, expressed as the soft-to-hard tissue movement ratio. COVARIATES: Covariates included age, sex, body mass index, mandibular plane angle, and soft tissue thickness. ANALYSES: Descriptive statistics were calculated. Student's t-test or nonparametric tests were used for appropriate group comparisons. Intraclass correlation coefficients assessed intrarater reliability. Spearman's correlation evaluated variable associations. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between microgenia severity and soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios. A two-tailed P value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The sample comprised 113 subjects with a mean age of 26.7 (4.4); 95 (84.01%) were female. Sagittal soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios ranged from 0.92 (0.13)-0.96 (0.09) to 0.63 (0.11)-0.70 (0.08) for patients with FCA ≤25 °, versus 0.98 (0.12)-1.03 (0.07) to 0.65 (0.07)-0.81 (0.11) in those with FCA>25 °. Intergroup comparison showed a statistically significant sagittal direction difference only at the menton [0.96 (0.09) vs 1.03 (0.07), P < .001]. Multivariable linear regression revealed microgenia severity had no independent association with soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios (all P > .05). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Analysis demonstrated stable soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios in both sagittal and vertical chin movements. The findings provide quantitative evidence facilitating more accurate models for predicting postoperative soft tissue outcomes.

item.title: High-volume cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma: development and external validation of an interpretable prediction model.

Authors: Wang D, Wang J, Wu Z, Cui Z
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963925
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transportability of models for postoperative high-volume cervical nodal disease in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and the incremental predictive value of molecular variables remain uncertain. METHODS: We developed models in the public Deyang cohort (521 patients; 90 events) and performed geographic external validation in the independent Liaocheng cohort (193 patients; 73 events). The outcome was >5 pathologically confirmed metastatic cervical lymph nodes. Five algorithms were compared using repeated stratified nested cross-validation with a prespecified 10-variable postoperative feature set. Ridge logistic regression (C = 0.1) was selected and applied without refitting. Paired comparisons of 8-variable clinicopathological and 10-variable clinicopathological-molecular models assessed the incremental value of high-risk co-mutation status and mutation count in both cohorts. RESULTS: Internal validation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.745-0.842), average precision (AP) of 0.497 (0.406-0.598), and Brier score of 0.115 (0.098-0.134). External AUROC was 0.752 (0.678-0.821), AP 0.601 (0.498-0.728), and Brier score 0.217 (0.180-0.254). Observed and mean predicted risks were 37.8% and 23.9%, respectively; the observed-to-expected ratio was 1.582 (1.319-1.860) and the weak-calibration slope was 0.831 (0.542-1.191). At the prespecified threshold of 0.158, sensitivity was 0.795 and specificity 0.600. Net benefit was 0.254 for the model and 0.261 for classifying all patients as high risk (difference, -0.008; 95% CI, -0.051 to 0.033). External paired differences after adding molecular variables were +0.002 for AUROC (-0.005 to 0.010), -0.002 for AP (-0.016 to 0.010), -0.001 for Brier score (-0.002 to 0.000), and +0.009 for net benefit (-0.003 to 0.026). CONCLUSION: The model retained moderate discrimination across centers but underestimated absolute risk and did not demonstrate a net benefit advantage over classifying all patients as high risk at the prespecified threshold. High-risk co-mutation status and mutation count showed no clear incremental predictive value. Further validation with standardized lymph-node assessment and patient outcomes is required before clinical application.

item.title: Immune-related adverse events are associated with favorable clinical outcomes in esophageal cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Fan J, Chen D, Jia L
item.description:
Authors: Fan J, Chen D, Jia L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1948772
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42903106



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. RESULTS: 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

item.title: Current Trends in Hemostatic Agents for Dental and Oral Surgical Procedures: A Narrative Review.

item.description:
Authors: Kim HJ, Jung K, Yang D

Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42901221



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Bleeding is a common concern in dental, oral, and maxillofacial surgery, particularly in patients with increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on local and systemic hemostatic agents, including their mechanisms, clinical applications, efficacy, and safety. METHODS: Literature published from January 2020 through November 2025 was reviewed using predefined search terms related to hemostatic agents and surgical bleeding. Clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, guidelines, and consensus statements were considered. Seven clinical cases were also reviewed to demonstrate practical applications of selected hemostatic agents. RESULTS: Mechanical agents provided effective control of routine bleeding, whereas active and flowable agents were useful for persistent or diffuse bleeding. Fibrin-based and combination approaches provided additional support in complex procedures. Tranexamic acid was particularly useful in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. CONCLUSION: Optimal hemostasis requires a tailored, procedure-specific strategy based on bleeding characteristics, surgical complexity, and patient-specific risk factors.

item.title: A Virtual Reality-Based Preoperative Operating Room Simulation for Patients Scheduled for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery: A Technical Innovation.

item.description:
Authors: Aijima R, Yamashita Y
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.09.023
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42901220



Abstract:
Patients scheduled for surgery under general anesthesia experience significant stress, including anxiety and fear, partly because of difficulty visualizing the operating room environment; however, preoperative visits to the operating room are often impractical. In oral and maxillofacial surgery, where many patients are young, perioperative anxiety and fear are particularly important issues, yet few studies have evaluated virtual reality (VR)-based operating room visits in this field. We developed a VR-based simulated operating room tour using a three-dimensional video camera to record the transport route from the hospital ward to the central operating room. Patients viewed the VR tour on the day before surgery and subsequently completed a questionnaire evaluating realism, satisfaction, ability to visualize the surgical experience, and changes in anxiety and fear. We describe this novel VR-based operating room tour as a feasible supplementary tool for preoperative patient orientation in oral and maxillofacial surgery.

item.title: Trends in Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use for Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism.
item.dc:creator: Varnier R, Bettega F, Moskal A, Mainbourg S, Wespiser M, Rousseau A, Viprey M
item.description:
Authors: Varnier R, Bettega F, Moskal A, Mainbourg S, Wespiser M, Rousseau A, Viprey M
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.40377
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42912389



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) are recommended for selected patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism, but their implementation remains heterogeneous. OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in DOAC initiation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in France and to identify factors associated with their use. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study included adults without recorded contraindications to DOACs and a first treated venous thromboembolism episode between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022. Data were collected from the French National Health Data System, a nationwide claims database covering approximately 99% of the population. Analysis was performed from January to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Patients were classified into active cancer and no active cancer groups. Covariates included calendar period, patient characteristics, cancer type and treatment, venous thromboembolism characteristics, and initial prescriber setting. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was DOAC initiation within 30 days after the index venous thromboembolism event. Bayesian structural time series models assessed temporal changes across 2016 to 2018, 2019 to 2020, and 2021 to 2022. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with DOAC initiation among patients with active cancer. RESULTS: Among 683 184 patients with incident treated venous thromboembolism (median [IQR] age, 67 [53-77] years; 347 421 female [51.0%]), 91 954 patients (13.5%) had active cancer while 591 230 (86.5%) had VTE not associated with active cancer. DOAC use increased from 15.3% (95% CI, 15.0%-15.7%) in 2016 to 2018 to 32.6% (95% CI, 32.1%-33.2%) in 2021 to 2022 among patients with active cancer, and from 63.5% (95% CI, 63.3%-63.7%) to 81.1% (95% CI, 80.9%-81.2%) among patients without active cancer. DOAC initiation increased beyond expected secular trends in patients with active cancer, with relative increases of 20.5% (95% credible interval, 13.0%-27.8%) in 2019 to 2020 and 41.3% (95% credible interval, 32.9%-50.2%) in 2021 to 2022. DOAC initiation was less frequent among patients with comorbidities, history of bleeding, gastrointestinal or gynecologic cancer, active brain metastases, or systemic treatment, and when the initial prescriber was a hospital-based physician rather than a general practitioner. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients with incident venous thromboembolism, DOAC use increased substantially in patients with active cancer but remained lower than in patients without active cancer and varied across clinical and care-setting characteristics. This lower uptake may reflect both delayed implementation of recent evidence and the need to individualize anticoagulant selection in complex situations.

Abstract:
Patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) have an unmet need for new therapies that improve survival. In this phase II trial, patients received ociperlimab and tislelizumab (A) or placebo and tislelizumab (B) (NCT04732494). The primary endpoint was not met, with an ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) assessed by the investigator of 30.6% (19.6-43.7) for A and 20.6% (11.5-32.7) for B (stratified risk difference: 9.9% [95% CI - 5.4 to 25.3]; stratified 2-sided p = 0.2114). item.title: Development-inspired approach for the derivation of functional and transplantable salivary gland organoids from human pluripotent stem cells.
item.dc:creator: Sherwood LJ, Samuel RZ, Bhamidipati SH, Nam K, Maslow F, Small T, Zhang Y, Wang J, Liu S, Baker OJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Sherwood LJ, Samuel RZ, Bhamidipati SH, Nam K, Maslow F, Small T, Zhang Y, Wang J, Liu S, Baker OJ, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77724-5
Published: 2026-Sep-17
PMID: 42897156



Abstract:
Salivary gland (SG) hypofunction significantly affects the life quality of patients with hyposalivation. Current treatment options for these conditions are limited and often result in undesirable side effects. To address this issue, we've developed a developmentally inspired strategy to derive salivary gland epithelial progenitor (SGEP) cells from human pluripotent stem cells (PSC). Then we employ SGEP cells derived from human PSC with a SOX10::GFP reporter to engineer three-dimensional lumenized SG organoids, with well-defined lumens and secretory function, reminiscent of human salivary glands. Upon transplantation into the submandibular gland of athymic nude mice, mCherry+ salivary gland organoids (SGO) integrate into the gland and differentiated into salivary gland phenotypes, including acinar, ductal and myoepithelial structures. Our findings suggest that SG organoids may hold promise for studying SG development, disease progression and drug screening, as well as for development of cell therapies for salivary gland regeneration.

item.title: Locoregional and distant recurrence after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a focused meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Ruan Y, Cao W, Long C, Li C, Han J
item.description:
Authors: Ruan Y, Cao W, Long C, Li C, Han J
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16944-w
Published: 2026-Sep-09
PMID: 42926222



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) is used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its effect on postoperative recurrence patterns remains uncertain. We compared overall, locoregional, and distant recurrence after NCIT versus neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT). METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 01 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with resectable or potentially resectable locally advanced ESCC who received NCIT or NCRT followed by radical esophagectomy. Recurrence outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs), and disease-free survival or recurrence-free survival (DFS/RFS) and overall survival (OS) as hazard ratios (HRs), using random-effects models. Post hoc sensitivity analyses excluded studies with marked between-group follow-up imbalance. RESULTS: Twenty comparative studies, all conducted in China, were included; 19 were retrospective observational studies and one was a randomized phase 2 trial. Five studies contributed to the overall-recurrence analysis, and six studies contributed to each of the locoregional- and distant-recurrence analyses. NCIT was associated with lower overall recurrence (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.03) and distant recurrence/metastasis (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.89; P = 0.009), whereas locoregional recurrence did not differ significantly (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.67-1.55; P = 0.92). In post hoc analyses excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, the locoregional estimate remained nonsignificant (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.15), and the distant-recurrence/metastasis estimate was attenuated and no longer significant (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.36-1.17). Ten studies contributed to OS, which favored NCIT (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93; P = 0.02; I² = 77%), whereas eight contributed to DFS/RFS, which did not differ significantly (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.59-1.13; P = 0.21; I² = 74%). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NCRT, NCIT was associated with fewer overall recurrences after radical esophagectomy for locally advanced ESCC. The primary distant-recurrence signal was not robust after excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, and no locoregional advantage was demonstrated. These findings do not establish therapeutic superiority and should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of retrospective evidence, risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity in survival analyses.

item.title: The areca (betel) nut: clinical implications for dental practice in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Desai T, Tungare S, Young S, Vigneswaran N, Quock RL, Myers AL
item.description:
Authors: Desai T, Tungare S, Young S, Vigneswaran N, Quock RL, Myers AL
Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.08.011
Published: 2026-Aug-26
PMID: 42919697



Abstract:
Areca nut (AN), commonly known as betel nut, has been used for centuries in ceremonies and rituals, consumed for unproven therapeutic effects, and abused as a recreational psychostimulant. AN is the fourth-most commonly abused psychoactive substance globally-only behind caffeine, nicotine, and alcohol-and its consumption is strongly associated with the development of adverse oral effects, most notably potentially malignant oral disorders (eg, oral leukoplakia and oral submucous fibrosis) and oral malignancies. Examples of other areca-related oral adverse reactions include profound dark brownish-blackish extrinsic staining, dentin hypersensitivity, periodontal disease, and betel chewer's mucosa. AN use is becoming more prevalent in Western countries, such as the United States, as a result of increasing immigration from regions where the habit is endemic-such as the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asians. However, US dental practitioners are likely unfamiliar with the habit and its significant clinical implications for oral health. Informing these practitioners is essential to identify users and to communicate effectively with them, along with managing the oral complications. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on AN use, with emphasis on US regulations and policy considerations, oral health effects, and findings from US-based studies of users of AN. Furthermore, we offer perspective about knowledge gaps (eg, increasing public awareness) and the ramifications for US dental practice.

item.title: A disease-specific immunonutritional model for prognostic stratification in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Su YS, Shen JH, Fang KH, Tsai MH, Kudva A, Lee YC, Huang EI, Tsai MS, Chang GH, Hsu CM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Su YS, Shen JH, Fang KH, Tsai MH, Kudva A, Lee YC, Huang EI, Tsai MS, Chang GH, Hsu CM, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16633-8
Published: 2026-Jul-25
PMID: 42919165



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) has demonstrated prognostic value across malignancies; however, its applicability to oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) remains uncertain. We aimed to develop a disease-specific immunonutritional model for prognostic stratification in surgically treated OCSCC, informed by the NPS framework. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 351 patients undergoing curative surgery for OCSCC (2009-2018). Survival-optimized cutoffs for albumin, total cholesterol, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio were determined using X-tile and integrated into a composite score (OCSCC-specific Naples Prognostic Score, OCNPS) to classify patients into three risk groups (Groups 0-2). Associations with overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: The proposed model stratified patients into distinct risk groups and was associated with adverse pathological features. Five-year OS rates were 81.2%, 63.4%, and 10.4% across Groups 0-2, whereas the original NPS did not discriminate between low- and intermediate-risk patients. In multivariable analyses, higher OCNPS categories independently predicted worse OS and DFS (Group 1: HR 1.63 and 1.42; Group 2: HR 6.46 and 6.66). A nomogram incorporating OCNPS improved prognostic discrimination compared with TNM staging (C-index 0.769 vs. 0.652) with good calibration. CONCLUSIONS: The OCNPS enables preoperative identification of patients with OCSCC at higher risk of adverse postoperative outcomes and provides clinically applicable prognostic information beyond conventional staging, supporting its potential role in OCSCC management.

item.title: Socioeconomic inequalities and the economic burden of dental caries: a longitudinal simulation analysis across forty countries.
item.dc:creator: Verma N, Dunleavy G, Stucke A, Jain S, de Rodrigues JM, Hofmeister J, Kebschull M, Chapple I, West N, Pitts N
item.description:
Authors: Verma N, Dunleavy G, Stucke A, Jain S, de Rodrigues JM, Hofmeister J, Kebschull M, Chapple I, West N, Pitts N
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28363-4
Published: 2026-Jul-24
PMID: 42897513



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, World Health Organization (WHO) member states endorsed the Bangkok declaration, prioritising oral diseases within universal health coverage and non-communicable disease agendas, and calling for prevention-oriented, primary care-led systems. This study aimed to: (1) explore the healthcare costs of managing dental caries between the ages of 12 and 65 years across income quintiles in 40 countries, and (2) estimate the potential reduction in direct costs from non-targeted and targeted oral health-promoting interventions. METHODS: A cohort simulation model was developed to estimate the direct costs of dental caries over time for different income quintiles across 40 countries. National-level DMFT (dentine threshold) data, the relative likelihood of receiving an intervention (such as a restorative procedure, tooth extraction and replacement), and clinically guided assumptions were used to populate the model. Private treatment costs in each country were used as a proxy to estimate the direct costs of dental caries. A hypothetical group of upstream and downstream preventive interventions were applied either uniformly across all income groups to reduce caries progression rates by 30% or in a "levelling-up" fashion with the greatest gains seen in the lowest income group. RESULTS: The population-level direct costs of caries from 12 to 65 years of age varied between US$317.8 million in Slovenia to US$182.6 billion in China. The highest per-person costs were in Switzerland at US$51,932 and the lowest in Jordan at US$6,339. The per-person direct costs were highest in the lowest income quintile 40 countries. Inadequate preventative oral care for lower income groups results in 50% higher total treatment costs. With the uniform application of preventive measures across all income quintiles, the greatest reduction in per-person costs for caries management was seen in the lowest income quintile across all countries. With a levelling-up approach, cost reductions in the lowest income group ranged from US$4,083 in Vietnam to US$43,106 in Switzerland. CONCLUSION: Lower income groups experience a greater health and economic burden from dental caries. Early, targeted preventive interventions, such as twice daily brushing with fluoridated toothpaste, water fluoridation, oral health education, and school programs, within a life-course, equity-driven framework, can reduce costs, mitigate disease burden, and advance global oral health equity.
